excerpt: Compare the actual inventory, setup work and cost over your intended stay. Furnished and unfurnished are starting descriptions; the agreement and condition record tell you what you are getting.
introduction:
A furnished apartment can look like the easy answer after an international move. You arrive with a suitcase and much of the setup appears to be done. An unfurnished home offers more choice, but the work of measuring, ordering and waiting for deliveries arrives at the same time as everything else.

The better option depends on what is included, how long you expect to stay and what you already own. Neither description has enough detail to make the decision on its own. Compare the homes as complete arrangements, including their contracts, condition and the practical cost of making them usable.
takeaways: Request an inventory rather than assuming what furnished or unfurnished includes.
Compare the same period and separate spending from refundable deposits.
Agree condition, repair responsibilities and what must be returned at the end.

sections.heading: Start with the contents, not the label
sections.body:
Ask for a written inventory of furniture, appliances, curtains, lighting and smaller items. A furnished home may include a bed but no bedding, a kitchen but limited cookware, or a desk that is unsuitable for regular work. An unfurnished home may still include some appliances and fitted storage. Inspect the actual unit rather than relying on photographs of a similar layout.

Check condition as well as presence. Sit on the seating, inspect storage, and ask to see appliances operating through an appropriate viewing or handover process. Record existing damage and missing items before occupation. A list saying that a washing machine exists does not explain whether it is working or who will arrange a repair.

Consider what you would need to remove or add. If you already own furniture, ask whether supplied pieces may be removed and where they would go. Do not assume the landlord will store them. Equally, a low setup budget is less convincing if several supposedly included items will need replacing immediately.

sections.heading: Separate furnishing from the type of agreement
sections.body:
A furnished home is not automatically a holiday home, and an unfurnished home is not a promise of any particular lease term. Establish whether you are comparing residential tenancies, serviced accommodation or holiday-home bookings. Duration, services and exit arrangements need to be read in the actual agreement.

For a Dubai residential tenancy, [DLD's registration and renewal service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/) sets out the Ejari process and applicable channels. A furnished inventory does not replace the tenancy paperwork. For accommodation operated as a Dubai holiday home, [DET's hospitality guidance](https://www.dubaidet.gov.ae/en/licences-and-permits/hospitality-services-and-permits) describes a different approval framework. Confirm which arrangement applies before comparing prices.

Ask who handles maintenance, cleaning, consumables and replacement of supplied items. Clarify the process for reporting damage and how the initial condition record will be agreed. If a promised service is important to the choice, obtain its scope in writing. A broad description such as fully serviced is not a detailed explanation of what happens when an appliance stops working.

Read extension, renewal and early-departure provisions carefully. A home that is easy to enter may still be expensive or inconvenient to leave. Your likely length of stay should be compared with those terms, rather than assuming furniture makes the commitment flexible.

sections.heading: Compare cost over the period you expect to stay
sections.body:
Build a simple comparison using the same duration for both options. Include rent or accommodation charges, setup purchases, delivery, assembly, storage and any known end-of-stay costs. Record utilities and other services separately where the inclusions differ. Refundable deposits affect initial cash needs, but should not be treated as consumed costs unless there is an actual deduction.

In the invented example below, an unfurnished option has AED 18,000 in setup spending and costs AED 1,000 less per month than the furnished option. Before other differences, twelve months of savings leave AED 6,000 of the setup amount unrecovered; twenty-four months produce AED 6,000 more savings than the initial setup spending. The simple crossover is eighteen months.

This is a sensitivity exercise, not a UAE rent quote. It ignores resale value, maintenance differences, financing, replacement costs and changes in rent. The result changes if any assumption changes. Use actual quotations and contract terms, and do not rely on recovering a particular resale value for your furniture.

sections.heading: Account for the work and the fit
sections.body:
A furnished option can reduce the number of deliveries and decisions immediately after arrival. That convenience has value if your work schedule is demanding or your stay is uncertain. It is less useful if the supplied layout makes everyday activities awkward or leaves no room for belongings that matter to you.

With an unfurnished home, measure both the rooms and the delivery route. A sofa that fits the living room may not fit the lift or entrance. Check lead times and assembly arrangements before choosing items, and leave enough space to move safely through the home while deliveries are incomplete.

Think about the less visible essentials: curtains, lamps, laundry equipment, bins and usable storage. These can consume time and money even when the main furniture budget looks reasonable. Our [first ninety days housing guide](/journal/moving-uae-first-90-days-housing) helps phase those decisions so the first week does not become a rushed attempt to finish every room.

If working from home is part of the plan, evaluate the actual desk position and room separation. A dining chair beside a decorative console is not automatically a workable office. The [home-working layout guide](/journal/working-from-home-uae-layout) provides a more focused viewing brief.

sections.heading: Agree the starting condition and the exit
sections.body:
At handover, compare the home with the inventory and record discrepancies together. Use clear photographs where appropriate, identify items precisely and retain the agreed record. Ask how faults discovered shortly after moving should be reported. Avoid signing a blanket statement that everything is satisfactory without completing the checks available to you.

For a furnished home, clarify whether items may be moved between rooms and what must be restored at departure. For an unfurnished home, check permissions for installations and the agreed condition on return. Wall-mounted furniture, curtains and other additions can involve responsibilities that should be understood before the work is done.

Make the final choice using the complete picture: cash needed now, likely stay, daily fit and exit obligations. The lowest advertised rent may create more setup work than you can manage; the most convenient furnished offer may cost more than its contents justify. A good comparison makes those tradeoffs explicit and lets you choose the arrangement that fits this stage of your life.
